drugRefs.why: Reliable CSF penetration and coverage of S. pneumoniae and N. meningitidis, the two dominant pathogens in community-acquired bacterial meningitis.
Added empirically to cover the possibility of ceftriaxone-resistant S. pneumoniae, given the high stakes of inadequate coverage in this disease.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Ceftriaxone + vancomycin covers the leading pathogens across most age groups; ampicillin must be added specifically for Listeria risk groups.
gaps: Listeria is not covered unless ampicillin is added — this is a common and dangerous omission in patients over 50 or immunocompromised.

stewardship.deescalation: Once CSF culture confirms the organism, narrow to the single most targeted agent — e.g., confirmed penicillin-susceptible S. pneumoniae allows discontinuation of vancomycin; confirmed N. meningitidis allows narrowing to penicillin G or ceftriaxone alone.

framework: Do not delay empiric antibiotics for lumbar puncture or imaging — give antibiotics immediately on clinical suspicion, then proceed to LP if safe and feasible.
Add ampicillin specifically for Listeria risk groups (age >50, pregnant, immunocompromised) — this is frequently missed and has serious consequences if omitted.
De-escalate promptly once CSF culture and Gram stain identify the specific organism and susceptibility.
